edges.fact: The posture corrector strap was described as super uncomfortable, like wearing a harness.
USER bought a posture corrector strap around late March.
USER ordered a pair of Vans Old Skools.
USER shared a similar experience of being measured at a shorter height than assumed with Kevin.
USER wore the posture corrector strap for about two weeks.
User has been consistent with wearing slim-fit henleys. They picked up two more in different colors last week. User finds slim-fit henleys to look better on them than anything loose.
User is going to the chiropractor twice a week for now. The chiropractor wants to do about eight sessions total and then reassess.
User is still going with 5'11¼" from their home measurement as their current height.
User mentioned Kevin, who had previously been measured at 5'8½". Kevin recently got measured at his new doctor and came in at 5'9". User doubts that Kevin actually grew.

User started seeing a chiropractor a couple weeks ago. The chiropractor did an initial assessment and took some X-rays of User's spine. The chiropractor said User has some mild compression in their thoracic region that could be contributing to a slight loss of height. The chiropractor is optimistic about the treatment plan.
User's chiropractor told them that after the alignment sessions, they should be measuring closer to 5'11½". The chiropractor says once the adjustments settle, that will be User's real height.
